The encoding of the latent variable determines the functions available to the model, while the unitary decides which combinations of them are seen by the trained layer. With the help of Pauli propagation we show that for a Clifford unitary each feature is a single product of sines and cosines of the encoded angles, so that a Clifford circuit, even a strongly entangling one, does not create new functions. Doping the circuit with $T$ gates mixes these products and changes the nonstabilizerness of the state, but the space of functions remains the one fixed by the encoding. For brickworks of Haar-random two-qubit gates the features are no longer single products, and their variation with the latent variable decreases with the depth of the circuit. For the proposed encoding and for one- and two-dimensional distributions, generated both from expectation values and from single measurements, neither the entanglement produced by a Clifford reservoir nor the additional nonstabilizerness of Haar-random brickworks systematically improves the generator, and a reservoir with no gates at all is competitive with entangling circuits.

papers.title_en: Exact decoherence dynamics of a detector coupled to vacuum fluctuations in bounded geometries
papers.abstract_en: The properties of quantum vacuum are highly sensitive to the underlying spacetime geometry and boundary conditions. We investigate in this paper the decoherence dynamics of a two-level system (detector) coupled to a vacuum scalar field through the $\hatσ_z$-coupling scheme under various boundary environments. By rigorously evaluating the reduced density matrix of the detector, we derive an exact general expression for the detector's decoherence function, $γ(Δt)$, and use it to characterize the dynamical decoherence of a detector in three scenarios: free space, a perfectly reflecting boundary, and a cavity formed by two parallel reflecting boundaries. We find that in free space the detector's coherence decays monotonically with time, indicating that vacuum fluctuations alone inevitably lead to a complete loss of coherence. In the single-boundary case, by contrast, the detector's coherence displays non-monotonic time evolution: $γ(Δt)$ increases with time up to a maximum and then settles to a steady value, indicating that the initial coherence can be partially preserved due to the presence of the boundary. When the detector is placed inside a cavity, its coherence evolution exhibits oscillatory behavior, and a significant fraction of the initial coherence survives. Moreover, for the same detector-boundary distance, more coherence is preserved in the cavity case than in the single-boundary case. These results provide a viable route for engineering quantum coherence via boundary conditions.

papers.title_en: Systematic calculations of β-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
papers.abstract_en: The process of $β$-delayed fission ($β$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $β$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $β$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $β$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $β$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $β$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $β$DF studies.

papers.title_en: Exclusive production of doubly charmed baryon pair at B Factories
papers.abstract_en: The exclusive production of doubly charmed baryon pairs $Ξ_{cc}+\barΞ_{cc}$ via $e^+e^-$ annihilation at B factories are calculated in the framework of non-relativistic QCD (NRQCD). The total cross sections, theoretical uncertainties, differential distributions and event yields for the BaBar and Belle II experiments are systematically discussed. According to our study, the detection prospects for both experiments are unfavorable.

papers.title_en: High significance measurement of reactor coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering on germanium by CONUS+
papers.abstract_en: We report the most precise measurement to date of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) from reactor antineutrinos using the CONUS+ high-purity germanium detectors at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields $1555 \pm 152$ CE$ν$NS events, with a significance of 10.2 $σ$, in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events within 0.6 standard deviations. The result also determines the weak mixing angle at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV, $\sin^2θ_W = 0.225 \pm 0.022$, consistent with the Standard Model prediction.

papers.title_en: Deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using frequency-converted photons emitted by a quantum dot
papers.abstract_en: Establishing secure communication is an important requirement in existing and future networks. Although current solutions rely on classical approaches, quantum mechanics offers the possibility of moving from computational to information-theoretic security. Quantum key distribution (QKD) has been extensively studied as a means of achieving such security. Recently, epitaxial quantum dots started to be studied and employed in quantum cryptography, because of their rapid development that made them one of the brightest sources of quantum light to date. In particular, they are known to be excellent sources of polarization-entangled photon pairs, especially droplet-etched dots operating at $\sim$780 nm. Here, we employ such a quantum dot to generate entangled photon pairs under 1 GHz excitation rate. Using quantum frequency conversion, we interface the emitted photons with the telecommunication wavelength range while preserving their polarization entanglement. This enables quantum key distribution over a 1.59 km field-deployed fibre link across the University of Stuttgart - campus Vaihingen, using the BBM92 protocol: we achieve a secure key rate of 206 Hz over 19 h of stable operation, resulting in a total secure key length of 14.2 Mbit. This key enables the safe encryption and decryption of a colour image with further implementation of error correction and privacy amplification. These results demonstrate important steps towards hybrid quantum networks by combining high-quality entangled-photon sources operated at high excitation rates, efficient frequency conversion module, and picosecond-level time synchronization in a realistic deployed network.

papers.title_en: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
papers.abstract_en: Feynman once remarked that the double-slit experiment has in its heart the only mystery of quantum mechanics. Arguably, the scientific significance of double-slit experiments lies in motional decoherence and the mechanism behind it. Decoherence of motional states underpins our understanding of quantum-to-classical transition. It is also central to the operation of miniaturized quantum electron devices and poses a resolution limit for electron microscopes. In this work, we provide experimental evidence for the critical role of quantum Brownian motion in electron motional decoherence. We demonstrate, for the first time, clear signatures of electron-metal decoherence and its continuous tunability. Our experiment concludes a two-decade long search for experimental realization of the Anglin-Paz-Zurek proposal, establishing electron-microchannel systems as viable open quantum platforms for free-electron quantum optics. The quantitative agreement between experiment and theory further paves the way for testing the Caldeira-Leggett quantum dissipation theory with free electrons.

papers.title_en: Precision measurement of the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ branching fraction and search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ at BESIII
papers.abstract_en: We present a precision measurement of the branching fraction of the rare decay $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$, and a search for a new gauge boson $Z^{\prime}$ that couples only to the second and third lepton generations, using a data sample of $(8998 \pm 39) \times 10^6$ $J/ψ$ events collected by the BESIII detector. The branching fraction of the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ decay is measured to be $B(J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-)=[0.91\pm0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.07~{\rm (syst.)}]\times 10^{-6}$, representing the most precise measurement to date and consistent with the theoretical prediction within one standard deviation. Additionally, we search for $CP$ asymmetry in the $J/ψ\toμ^+μ^-μ^+μ^-$ decay and determine the T-odd observable to be $A_T = [0.05\pm 0.04~{\rm (stat.)}\pm0.01~{\rm (syst.)}]$, which is consistent with $CP$ conservation. In the search for $J/ψ\to Z^{\prime}μ^+μ^-$ via $Z^{\prime}\toμ^+μ^-$, no significant $Z^{\prime}$ signal is observed in the $μ^+μ^-$ invariant mass region of $(0.212,~2.6)$~GeV$/c^2$, and we set upper limits on the ${\rm U}(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model coupling constant $g^{\prime}$ ranging from 0.001 to 0.294 at the 90% confidence level, which is comparable to the upper limits set by Belle II for $Z^{\prime}$ masses below $0.7$~GeV$/c^2$.

papers.title_en: Homodyne Unravelling and Parameter Estimation in Squeezed Thermal Baths
papers.abstract_en: We derive an alternative formulation of the stochastic master equation describing the evolution of quantum systems continuously measured via homodyne detection in a squeezed-thermal environment. This formulation allows us to identify two distinct collapse operators, corresponding respectively to the monitored and unmonitored channels, and to express the quantum state evolution directly in terms of Kraus-like operators. As a consequence, it facilitates the application of advanced numerical methods that account for higher-order corrections and discrete-time monitoring, and it also enables the efficient numerical evaluation of Cramér-Rao bounds in parameter estimation problems. To demonstrate the latter, we evaluate the Fisher information of the continuous homodyne monitoring for qubit frequency estimation in the presence of a squeezed-thermal bath. Our results show that exponential scaling of the steady-state Fisher information rate with squeezing is retained even at non-zero temperature.

papers.title_en: Measurement incompatibility and noiseless quantum codes
papers.abstract_en: We construct a rank-one minimal informationally complete measurement (MIC) with an invertible dual operator and prove that, for arbitrary finite input and output dimensions, a channel universally preserves measurement incompatibility if and only if its input space contains a noiseless code subspace of the full output dimension. Preserving the compatibility threshold of a finite family of binary measurements already guarantees such a code. Furthermore, for every $d\ge2$, there exists a family of binary measurements that is incompatible on the full space but compatible after compression to any proper subspace. These results resolve the conjecture of Chitambar and Zhang and the existence question posed by Uola and coauthors. We also give an explicit construction of exact encodings and show that, for a sufficiently small shift in the compatibility threshold, the transmission error of an approximate encoding is bounded by a constant times the square of the shift. These results establish a connection between measurement compatibility, quantum steering, and quantum error correction.

papers.title_en: Security Analysis of Ekert-type QKD Protocol Coming Under Cloning Attacks
papers.abstract_en: We analyze the security of an Ekert type bipartite key distribution protocol coming under cloning attacks by an untrusted observer. Precisely, an eavesdropper is assumed to intercept and apply an asymmetric, phase-variant cloner on one or both qubits which are transmitted over public channel from an authenticated source to the trusted parties. We partially characterize two-qubit states from the perspective of designing a QKD protocol that can generate a distillable secret key among the trusted users even under such cloning attacks. We rely upon Devetak Winter framework for computing key rate so as to identify states, which when used in the protocol, secret-key can be distilled. Utility of an entangled state, for designing a successful QKD protocol, changes from single-qubit to double-qubits cloning attacks. Interestingly, we can distinguish some useful families of two-qubit entangled states when only one of the transmitted qubits is cloned by a malicious third party.

papers.title_en: Prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution from a bound on information leakage
papers.abstract_en: Every quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol must limit the information available outside the users' laboratories. In device-independent QKD this is essentially the only assumption made on the devices. In a prepare-and-measure setting it cannot be imposed strictly, since the sender's device must emit a signal that depends on her private input. The natural replacement, and a minimal one, is a leakage bound: a bound on how much information about the input leaves the sender's laboratory, through the intended signal or through any side channel. We ask how far this unavoidable requirement can replace a detailed model of the source. We show that this single bound, quantified by the probability of guessing the input from everything the source emits, suffices to prove security against collective attacks. In our analysis, nothing is assumed about the precise form of the emitted states, their dimension, energy or purity, nor about the receiver's measurement device, beyond the standard requirement that it does not leak Bob's data. The standard B92 and BB84 protocols do not certify any key under this minimal leakage bound assumption. But closely related protocols can and, in the ideal limit, achieve one secret bit per key round. For noisy implementations, we compute key rates using semidefinite programming relaxations. Our best protocols tolerate visibilities down to 0.84, corresponding to an 8% quantum bit error rate, compared with the 11% threshold of standard device-dependent BB84.

papers.title_en: Global Analysis of Nuclear Parton Distribution Functions using Markov Chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract_en: Global analyses of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) have traditionally used the Hessian method for uncertainty estimation, relying on a local quadratic approximation of the chi-squared function. This Gaussian approximation can be inadequate when experimental constraints are limited and parameter correlations are strong, as it cannot fully capture asymmetric uncertainties, flat directions, or multiple minima. This thesis develops a Bayesian framework for nPDF determination using Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques within the nCTEQ analysis framework. An adaptive Metropolis-Hastings algorithm enables direct sampling of the posterior distribution, revealing pronounced non-Gaussian behavior and secondary minima, particularly in the valence distributions. The analysis presents the first global single-nucleus determination of lead (Pb) PDFs based exclusively on lead data, complemented by a multi-nuclei analysis incorporating different nuclear targets through a standard analytic dependence on the mass number. Including lighter nuclei significantly constrains quark distributions and changes the extracted lead PDFs, while the gluon distribution remains comparatively stable. A comparison with Hessian-based results highlights the limitations of the Gaussian approximation in regions with strong nonlinearity or multimodality. Overall, this work establishes Bayesian MCMC inference as a flexible framework for nPDF determination, providing a more comprehensive characterization of parameter uncertainties and the underlying parameter space.

papers.title_en: Measurement of spectator fragment pseudorapidity distributions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
papers.abstract_en: At sufficiently low center-of-mass energies, charged particles originating from the spectator region fall within the pseudorapidity acceptance ($2.14<|η|<5.09$) of the STAR Event Plane Detector (EPD). Measurements of the pseudorapidity distributions of helium spectator fragments are presented for Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{_{\mathrm{NN}}}}=$ 19.6, 14.6, 11.5, 9.2, and 7.7 GeV. The helium fragment yields in each EPD ring are extracted from fits to the deposited energy spectra using convoluted Landau distributions while accounting for the contribution from singly charged particles. The effects of the EPD detection efficiency and interactions of the fragments with the STAR beam pipe are evaluated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting pseudorapidity distributions are presented as a function of collision energy and collision centrality.

papers.title_en: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
papers.abstract_en: The "Rayleigh limit" is not an intrinsic property of light, but a consequence of sub-optimal measurement of collected photons by the imaging instrument. To overcome this limitation, we present Adaptive Information Mining, a framework that achieves super-resolution by using sequentially refined measurements for incoming photons. Our approach employs a reconfigurable imaging system that dynamically reshapes the instrument measurement responses to maximize the Fisher information and guide scene estimation toward the fundamental quantum limit, even in deep sub-Rayleigh regimes. We demonstrate that this approach achieves an estimation error 2-5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging when imaging point sources, without requiring any prior knowledge of their positions and brightnesses. Importantly, we demonstrate that AIM can be extended to fully blind multi-parameter estimation in scenarios involving an unknown number of sources or turbulence-induced wavefront distortions. Our approach addresses the limitations of conventional fixed imaging, offering a practical path toward quantum-limited super-resolution imaging.

papers.title_en: On-shell Mass Renormalisation and RG-improved Effective Potential in Vector-like Lepton Models
papers.abstract_en: We discuss the on-shell mass renormalisation in a class of six vector-like lepton (VLL) extensions of the Standard Model with seesaw-like contributions to the SM lepton masses. The schemes absorb large radiative corrections to the SM lepton masses arising from mixing between the SM and VLLs with up to $5\times5$ mixing matrices and allows for efficient computation of observables and the low-scale $\overline{\text{MS}}$ values of model parameters. We determine and solve the redundancy-free 2-loop renormalisation-group (RG) equations, compute the RG-improved effective potential and study the vacuum instability scales of each of the VLL models. We find rich phase behaviour and parameter regions that show instability scales as low as $10^5$ GeV as well as regions where the one-loop corrections to the input parameters can lead to a stable vacuum.

papers.title_en: Color-Reconnection Effects on the nMPI-Nch Conditional Multiplicity Fluctuations in PYTHIA 8 pp Collisions
papers.abstract_en: We examine conditional charged-multiplicity fluctuations at fixed multiparton interaction (MPI) count in retained PYTHIA proton-proton samples at centre-of-mass energies of 2.76, 7, and 13 TeV. Charged particles satisfy |eta| < 0.8 and 0.15 < pT < 20 GeV/c. In the historical colour-reconnection (CR)-labelled baseline samples, the CR-ON conditional mean is smaller by a larger fraction than the standard deviation: the absolute width is smaller, while the coefficient of variation is larger in every retained matched MPI bin. Effective lifetime/decay settings and their per-run correspondence are unverified for this baseline, so these comparisons do not establish that CR alone causes the observed differences or their energy dependence. A separately documented 13 TeV comparison using the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) CP5 tune, with equal non-CR physics settings and particle data across the ON/OFF pair, exhibits the same absolute-versus-relative width ordering. Retained independent Monash and A14 samples also show this pattern, subject to historical production-record limitations. A comparison with mean-transverse-momentum data from A Large Ion Collider Experiment (ALICE) and simulated activity estimators provides final-state context within the stated particle-definition and provenance limits.

papers.title_en: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$ν$NS measurement
papers.abstract_en: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$ν$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$ν$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$ν$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1555 \pm 152$ CE$ν$NS events, corresponding to a significance of 10.2$\,σ$. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.91 \pm 0.14$.

papers.title_en: Search for Neutrino-Produced Long-Lived Particles Using the SBND Cosmic Ray Tagger Beam Telescope
papers.abstract_en: The Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) is a liquid argon time projection chamber in Fermilab's Short-Baseline Neutrino Program, positioned 110 meters from the neutrino target along the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB). In addition to its neutrino physics goals, SBND enables searches for new physics, including long-lived particles (LLPs) produced via neutrino-nucleus upscattering that decay into visible final states. Although neutrino data taking with the full SBND experiment began in December 2024, a subset of the Cosmic Ray Tagger (CRT) system operated from 2017--2018 as a standalone detector, referred to as the CRT Beam Telescope, collecting data corresponding to $2.95\times 10^{20}$ protons on target from the BNB. Originally intended for commissioning and performance studies, the substantial dataset collected also enables searches for displaced LLP decays. This paper presents the first search for physics beyond the Standard Model using data from the SBND CRT Beam Telescope, targeting LLP decays into electron-positron pairs. We observe no significant excess above the expected background and set 90% confidence-level upper limits on an effective production cross section at the level of $10^{-38}$ cm$^2$ for laboratory decay lengths of 0.3-100 m. These results complement existing searches by probing displaced decay signatures at meter-scale decay lengths.

papers.title_en: Electron-to-Muon Forward Annihilation at High Energy
papers.abstract_en: We study the high-energy behavior of electron-to-muon annihilation in forward kinematics in QED with two massive lepton species. Using effective field theory renormalization group techniques we derive the all-order asymptotic behavior of the annihilation amplitude through the next-to-leading logarithmic approximation. Furthermore, we consider one- and two-loop fixed-order corrections to the forward-annihilation amplitude in the high-energy limit, which we compute up to power corrections. The goal of this paper is to elaborate on various technical details that we omitted in the original presentation of our results in arXiv:2510.04914.

papers.title_en: Using Higgs Boson Production in Association with Three Jets via Gluon Fusion at the LHC to Investigate the CP Properties of the Higgs Boson
papers.abstract_en: A neutral Higgs boson $Φ$ with general scalar and pseudoscalar couplings and accompanying jets can be efficiently produced via gluon fusion through heavy-quark loops in high-energy hadronic collisions. We present integrated cross sections and kinematic distributions for the production of a generic Higgs boson $Φ$ in association with three jets, $pp \to Φjjj$, at order $α_{s}^{5}$. We include the full mass dependence of the top- and bottom-quark loop contributions, combined coherently so that their interference is retained. Earlier finite-mass calculations of $Φ+3$ jets with bottom-quark loops and $CP$-odd or $CP$-mixed couplings were restricted to $gg \to gggΦ$; we include the complete set of partonic subprocesses, and find that the quark-containing channels supply close to one half of the pseudoscalar three-jet cross section at $\tanβ=1$. In a Type-II two-Higgs-doublet model the bottom-quark loop comes to dominate the rate as $\tanβ$ is increased, so that the cross section is non-monotonic in $\tanβ$. Comparing against the heavy-top effective theory and its form-factor-improved version, we show that the effective description fails in the hard tails of the transverse-momentum and dijet-mass distributions, while the third-jet centrality $z^\star$ and the rapidity separation of the two leading jets are largely insensitive to the heavy-quark treatment. We further study the multi-jet azimuthal correlation $Φ_{2}$, built from the jet momenta on the two sides of the Higgs boson in rapidity, and find that the bottom-quark contribution modifies its shape even for a state of definite $CP$. For a $CP$-mixed state the interference of the two couplings adds a $\sin2Φ_2$ term, which a simple counting asymmetry isolates and which no $CP$ eigenstate can produce. Numerical results are presented for the LHC at $\sqrt{s}=13.6~$TeV and $m_Φ=125.2~$GeV.

papers.title_en: Dynamical quantum simulations as laboratories for quantum information
papers.abstract_en: Dynamical quantum simulations are commonly designed to access a particular response function or correlation function. Yet the underlying protocol prepares a family of many-body states that contains information well beyond the observable for which the simulation was originally designed. In this work, we explore the idea of using these states as laboratories for quantum information. As a case study, we consider the local-pulse protocols used to compute Green functions in finite XX and XXX spin chains, and we interpret opposite source rotations as encoding a classical bit into the many-body system. This allows us to follow how the resulting record propagates, how it is encoded across local subsystems, and how readily it can be accessed with different measurements. We also find a clear separation between representation and readout. While fermionic covariance data exactly reconstruct the signed response in the XX chain, simple spin measurements recover a larger fraction of the locally available information in the XXX chain. This reversed ordering persists when we move from finite-pulse discrimination to local source-angle estimation. Going beyond the source record, the same reduced states also allow us to reinterpret results in terms of Bell state recovery and quantum communication rates, as well as providing direct access to the evolving bipartite and genuine multipartite entanglement of the system. Our results show that dynamical quantum simulations developed for response calculations can naturally be used to ask a much broader set of quantum-information questions about the many-body states they already prepare.

papers.title_en: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
papers.abstract_en: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.

papers.title_en: Descartes Curvature Geometry, Compact-Cycle Amplitudes, and the GST Cabibbo Seed
papers.abstract_en: Several apparently distinct formulations of the charged-lepton mass relation $p_2/e_1^2 = 2/3$ share a common algebraic object: the ratio of flavor-breaking to flavor-symmetric amplitude components on an internal family space. We show that (i) the relation expressed as a Fourier-mode constraint on Shulga's compact cycle, (ii) the same relation as a Descartes curvature condition in the sense of Kocik, and (iii) the Soddy completion of the resulting circle configuration are related by exact algebra, with no approximations. The Soddy completion defines a companion scale $F^2 = α^2 μ_\star$ with $α= \sqrt{3/2} - 1$ and $μ_\star = \sum_\ell m_\ell$; identifying this scale with $\bar{m}^{\rm MS}_s(μ_\star)$ yields a light-quark mass cascade with the ratio $m_d/m_s = 5/2 - \sqrt{6}$. Combined with the leading Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation, this gives the down-sector Cabibbo seed $\sqrt{m_d/m_s} = \sqrt{3/2} - 1 = 0.22474\ldots$, numerically close to the measured $|V_{us}| = 0.22503 \pm 0.00068$ ($0.4σ$). A full CKM evaluation requires the up-sector phase correction, which we defer. The correspondence is testable by future lattice QCD+QED determinations of $m_d/m_s$; explicit failure modes are listed.

papers.title_en: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
papers.abstract_en: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

papers.title_en: Lower Bound for Region of Non-Distillable Magic States
papers.abstract_en: Magic states are a leading proposal for realizing fault-tolerant and universal quantum computation. At the present moment, much of the theory of magic states is not understood. Even simple questions such as what single qubit states have magic remain open. In Campbell and Browne's seminal paper on bound magic states, they prove the existence of states outside of the stabilizer octahedron which cannot be used to achieve universal computation. In this paper we expand upon their proof and determine a lower-bound on this region.

papers.title_en: Twisted Fourier Analysis of Quantum Weight Enumerators
papers.abstract_en: A unified Fourier framework for quantum weight enumerators of prime-power-dimensional qudits is developed in this paper. We introduce the notions of Weyl power spectrum and Weyl-conjugation autocorrelation for the Weyl-operator quantities nderlying the Shor--Laflamme weight enumerators. Representing these quantities as formal vectors, we show that they form a symplectic Fourier transform pair, from which the quantum MacWilliams identity follows by applying the Hamming-weight functional. This framework extends to a family of twisted Fourier transforms, including the Rains shadow transform. We show that identical-copy Bell sampling corresponds to a twisted autocorrelation related to the shadow enumerator through Weyl translation and Hamming projection. We further prove that all twisted Fourier transforms are Weyl translations of either the ordinary MacWilliams transform or the Rains shadow transform. This two-class reduction implies that the twists yield no additional independent coefficientwise positivity constraints under compatible projections. Nevertheless, the framework leads to refined MacWilliams and shadow identities that retain more Fourier information than ordinary Hamming weight enumerators. We employ these refined identities in linear programming, together with simplex mapping and shadow-coset counting, to exclude surviving candidate weight distributions. These techniques yield tighter bounds for binary and qutrit quantum codes, including nonexistence results for specific code parameters.

papers.title_en: Perspective on AI and quantum open-source software
papers.abstract_en: Quantum open-source software provides essential infrastructure for quantum science, and artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping its capabilities and transforming its development. However, verifying quantum software at scale remains difficult, and AI-generated contributions can increase the workload of maintainers. In this Perspective, we examine verification as a central requirement for reliable AI-assisted quantum software development and research. We analyze public repositories, records covering 110 repositories from five annual quantum open-source hackathons that we organize, and responses from more than 1600 participants in a community survey. Our analysis connects limitations in automated verification with the review burden on quantum software maintainers. We propose verification practices and contribution standards that require contributors to support their changes with reproducible evidence for maintainer review. We also examine how quantum open-source software can provide infrastructure for AI-driven research whose results the community can independently verify and build upon. We maintain an open-source companion repository to support reproducibility and help projects adopt and refine these proposals. Together, these contributions help the quantum open-source software community translate advances in AI into reliable quantum research through reproducible verification.

papers.title_en: Self-Synchronized Soft X-Ray and Infrared Free-Electron Lasers from a Single Prebunched Electron Beam
papers.abstract_en: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy combining intense infrared and x-ray pulses is an important tool for investigating complex structural and electronic dynamics in materials. However, current configurations combining external sources and x-ray free-electron lasers (FELs) often suffer from high system complexity, inherent timing jitter, or limited pulse properties. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the generation of intrinsically synchronized soft x-ray (SXR) and midinfrared (MIR) FELs from a single prebunched electron beam. Sequentially passing the beam through an SXR undulator followed by an MIR amplifier reveals a highly synergistic process: the initial periodic MIR density modulation boosts the SXR FEL pulse energy, while robustly surviving the intense SXR FEL to drive high-power, narrowband MIR radiation. Extending this scheme to lower terahertz frequencies suppresses SXR power, but this can be compensated by machine tuning. Originating from the same electron bunch, the dual-color pulses inherently maintain a precise, constant time delay. This intrinsically synchronized scheme establishes a highly reliable platform tailored for both SXR-pump and infrared-probe and infrared-pump and SXR-probe experiments.

papers.title_en: Gauge-Field Production in Axion Inflation
A microRWELL-based preshower and muon system for the IDEA detector
Schwinger Pair Creation by a Time-Dependent Electric Field in de Sitter Space with the Energy Density E_μ E^μ=E^2 a^2(τ)
Large Language Models for Quantum Code Translation: An Exploratory Study
papers.abstract_en: Quantum software development is challenged by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented software development kits (SDKs), which complicate cross-SDK code translation and execution. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based approach for translating executable programs between high-level quantum SDKs. We develop a quantum-aware translation workflow whose prompt design and validation reflect quantum semantics and accommodate the version evolution of quantum ecosystems. We conduct a preliminary evaluation of 4 LLM configurations on 43 tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q#. LLMs achieve a zero-shot Pass@1 of up to 72.33%, while one-shot prompting further improves the translation effectiveness. These results suggest potential for quantum code translation by LLMs.

papers.title_en: From Single Spins to Ensembles: A Calibrated Symbolic Regression Pipeline for NV Spectroscopy
papers.abstract_en: Characterizing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensembles requires connecting their collective spectra to individual centers that experience different local environments. We develop a symbolic-regression pipeline that carries single-center spin structure into a calibrated ensemble model by generating individual spectral responses and combining them with explicit weights. A constrained search selects Hermitian operator terms from single-center optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, fits their coefficients, and retains the selected expressions as source models for the ensemble. Ensemble calibration then accounts for resonance shifts, local disorder, orientation, and optical response while keeping the individual spectral contributions accessible. On public single-center and ensemble data, the zero-field ensemble held-frequency root-mean-square error decreases from 0.008835 to 0.003872 in normalized photoluminescence, a 56.2% improvement over matched uncorrected composition. In controlled QuTiP ensembles of 128 sites spanning four NV orientations, models calibrated at 0 and 3 mT predict an independently held-out 5.17 mT spectrum with errors of 0.000207-0.000228 across three random seeds, comparable to the 0.000200 noise standard deviation. Resolving the simulated response into its individual-center contributions shows how local spectral diversity combines into the ensemble line shape. By retaining the source Hamiltonians while calibrating sample-dependent spectral differences, the pipeline connects local spin physics to collective optical readout and makes the contributions to an ensemble line shape available for physical interpretation.

papers.title_en: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fejér kernel
papers.abstract_en: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fejér kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.

papers.title_en: Rank-one Factored Gradient Descent without Restricted Isometry: Application to Quantum Pure State Tomography on Multi-Qubits
papers.abstract_en: Factored gradient descent (FGD) is a scalable nonconvex method for low-rank positive semidefinite matrix recovery, in which the rank and positivity constraints are satisfied automatically by the factorization. Most of the existing theory that certifies benignity of its loss landscape, however, relies on a restricted isometry property (RIP) of the measurement map. In quantum state tomography, one of its applications, the measurements that can be acquired with stable statistics are limited by detection efficiency and drift to Pauli observables of low weight; we first show that under such partial-weight Pauli measurements RIP fails in the worst possible way. We then bundle the mutually commuting observables setting by setting, pushing the state forward to the probability distribution of each setting, and introduce a max-sliced total-variation loss. On the stratum where the setting attaining the maximum is unique there is no spurious local minimum, and provided only that the measurement map is injective on generic pure states, the global minimum is the truth up to a phase. Finally we verify these claims numerically on four qubits and compare against FGD with the ordinary loss.

papers.title_en: Membership in the cone of quantum states over time is NP-hard
papers.abstract_en: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $ρ$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(ρ\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. Characterizing the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ these operators generate was posed as an open problem in~\cite{HoogstederCalsamigliaWinter2025}. We exhibit a linear copy of the bipartite separable cone as an exposed face of $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$: for output systems of the form $B = A'R$ with $A'$ a copy of the input, there is an explicit witness $W_0\in\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}^*$ and an explicit injective linear map $L$ with $σ\in \mathrm{SEP}_{+}(A{:}R)\iff L(σ)\in\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}(A{:}A'R)$. Composing with the NP-hardness of separability shows that exact membership, weak membership, and weak optimization are NP-hard for $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ and its dual. A quantitative stability bound makes the weak-membership reduction valid at inverse-polynomial accuracy. Thus polynomial-time membership tests do not exist unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Independently of this complexity assumption, Fawzi's theorem implies that $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}(A{:}A'R)$ admits no finite semidefinite representation when $d=\dim A\ge2$, $r=\dim R\ge2$, and $d+r>5$.

papers.title_en: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
papers.abstract_en: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.

papers.title_en: Geometric aspects of fault tolerance
papers.abstract_en: We highlight three geometric aspects of fault tolerance. First, we construct an operator-algebraic formulation of the fiber bundle framework for fault tolerance, and show that a generalization of the Knill-Laflamme conditions implies a flat connection for this framework. Next, we develop this framework for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We show that, for each polarization type, their moduli space embeds smoothly into a Grassmannian of finite-dimensional subspaces of a regularized distribution space. Finally, we explain how GKP codes associated with Jacobians give rise to magic states that can be obtained by code space projections of Gaussian states and identify a $\rm CCZ$-type magic state arising this way.

papers.title_en: Benchmarking quantum-annealing-based approaches for factory layout planning
papers.abstract_en: The earlystage of factory layout planning has a direct effect on the operating costs, efficiency, and productivity of manufacturing systems. Conventional automated planning approaches often face a trade-off between solution quality and computational effort. Recent studies have investigated the potential of quantum annealing (QA) for solving factory layout planning problems. However, existing studies have mainly focused on individual QA-based formulations, whereas current hybrid QA solvers support multiple model types that combine QA and classical methods. To explore the potential of QA for factory layout planning, this paper benchmarks four QA based approaches implemented with the corresponding solvers, including an iterative binary quadratic model (IBQM), a hybrid discrete quadratic model (HDQM), a hybrid constrained quadratic model (HCQM), and a hybrid nonlinear model (HNLM). To improve scalability, an iterative decomposition strategy is developed for IBQM, while a candidate selection procedure is introduced for HDQM. The approaches are benchmarked against genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization, and a hybrid tabu search and simulated annealing approach on 14 layout instances with different layout sizes, geometric complexity, spatial restrictions, and transport route configurations. The comparative analysis considers solution quality, computation time, and scalability. The results show that QA-based approaches achieve competitive solution quality and substantial computational advantages, reducing computation time by up to 94.51% relative to the classical reference methods. Among them, IBQM obtains the best solution quality in 78.6% of the instances, with a maximum improvement of 17.41% associated with an 81.34% reduction in computation time. These findings provide a basis for their further application in industrial layout planning.

papers.title_en: Complete entropy contraction from conditional hyperboundedness
papers.abstract_en:
For finite-dimensional quantum channels compatible with a faithful conditional expectation, we show that conditional hyperboundedness and strict GNS contraction together yield a relative entropy contraction. For KMS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups, a conditional $2\to q$ hyperboundedness at time $t_0>0$ combined with a GNS gap $λ>0$ implies a modified logarithmic Sobolev constant 
\[ α=\frac{λ(1-2/q)} {12(λt_0+\log M+1-2/q)},\]
 where $M$ is the hyperboundedness constant. As a consequence, completely bounded hyperboundedness over auxiliary systems gives complete versions of entropy contraction with the same rates.

papers.title_en: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
papers.abstract_en: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.

papers.title_en: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
papers.abstract_en: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^λ_F(ρ)\}_{λ>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.

papers.title_en: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract_en: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

papers.title_en: Nonabelian Higgs fields from minimal submanifolds
papers.abstract_en: We construct $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang-Mills-Higgs fields on a broad class of noncompact Riemannian manifolds, concentrating in the large-mass limit along prescribed nondegenerate minimal submanifolds of codimension three. The solutions have uniformly bounded rescaled energy. On closed manifolds with $b_1(M)=0$, adding a suitably scaled Higgs potential gives an analogous concentration result. Our construction completes one direction of the correspondence proposed by Parise, Pigati and Stern, realising prescribed minimal submanifolds of codimension three as concentration sets of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Higgs fields.

Based on a sample of $(2712.4 \pm 14.3) \times 10^6$$ψ(3686)$ events collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, we report the first observation of the decays $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{+} Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.$ and $ψ(3686)\to\bar{p} K^{*}(892)^{0} Σ^{+} + c.c.$. The corresponding branching fractions are determined to be $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}K^+Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}+c.c.)=(3.94\pm0.15_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.24_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$ and $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}Σ^++c.c.)=(4.93\pm0.14_{\text{stat.}}\pm0.30_{\text{syst.}})\times10^{-5}$. Furthermore, we search for the hidden-strange pentaquark candidates $N_{x}(1875)$ and $N_{x}(2100)$ in the invariant mass spectra of $K^{+} Σ^{*}(1385)^{0}$ and $K^{*}(892)^{0} Σ^{+}$, respectively. No significant signals are observed and the upper limits on the branching fractions at the 90% confidence level are $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(1875)\to\bar{p}K^+Σ^{*}(1385)^{0})<1.58\times10^{-6}$ and $\mathcal{B}(ψ(3686)\to\bar{p}N_{x}(2100)\to\bar{p}K^{*}(892)^{0}Σ^+)<3.09\times10^{-7}$.

papers.title_en: A General Framework for Leggett--Garg Violation in Neutrino Oscillations and Matter Effects
papers.abstract_en: The Leggett--Garg inequality (LGI) constrains temporal correlations under the assumptions of macrorealism and noninvasive measurability. We study the four-time quantity \(K_4\) for two-flavor neutrino oscillations using a pseudo-density matrix (PDM) under static conditions, instead of non-invasive measurement. With this approach, it becomes possible to examine a Horodecki-type criterion for the temporal Pauli-correlation tensor. The Horodecki criterion had been proven for CHSH inequality (R. Horodecki et al. Phys. Lett. \textbf{A200}, 340), For any unitary qubit evolution, the corresponding scalar is \(M_R=2\). Although, this result characterizes the correlation tensor and the optimized temporal construction, it does not imply that a fixed flavor observable violates the LGI at every neutrino energy or baseline. We therefore evaluate \(K_4\) explicitly for flavor measurements in matter of constant density. The numerical examples illustrate how matter effects modify the temporal correlations, with a pronounced matter--vacuum separation near the MSW resonance for the chosen parameters and generally smaller differences in the selected off-resonance cases. This finding motivates further investigation of matter-induced temporal correlations in atmospheric neutrinos and their potential relevance to future studies with long-baseline and atmospheric-neutrino experiments, including DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande.

papers.title_en: Target Detection with Asymmetric Gaussian Classical Correlation
papers.abstract_en: We study the characteristics of two-mode classical correlation in Gaussian regime, which is produced by impinging a thermal state into a beam splitter. It is explicitly investigated how a measurement on one mode affects the other. The result enables the distinction between classical and quantum correlations. Then, we show how classically correlated states are advantageous in target detection, specifically for an asymmetric classical correlation with different mean photon numbers in the signal and idler modes. Under on-off detection, the classically correlated states significantly outperform quantum correlated states as the environmental thermal mean photon number increases. Furthermore, we demonstrate the advantage of local Gaussian operations in the target detection.

papers.title_en: Quantum ordinal selection with two comparisons
papers.abstract_en: We study the optimal probability of selecting an object within a prescribed rank threshold using at most two noiseless coherent pairwise comparisons of an unknown strict order. Polynomial degree bounds alone can overestimate the success attainable with two comparisons. We develop a comparison-specific semidefinite model that completely characterizes attainable success. Computer-assisted proofs establish the exact optimum for every rank threshold at seven objects and for minimum selection at eight. For minimum selection, we construct an explicit algorithm family and determine its exact optimum. Bounds for all admissible two-comparison algorithms show that the family's asymptotic success is within 0.016% of the unrestricted optimum. We also prove that this relative gap has a strictly positive limit. The optimal quantum-to-classical success ratio for minimum selection converges to approximately 2.48 under the same two-comparison budget.

papers.title_en: Neutrinos as Quantum Information Carriers? A Gap Analysis Against the DiVincenzo Criteria
papers.abstract_en: Photons, trapped ions, neutral atoms, and superconducting circuits are all well-known quantum information platforms. Neutrinos offer a unique possibility, displaying quantum interference (flavour oscillation) over thousands of kilometres, yet interacting so weakly that they can travel through the Earth with minimal interaction. This short paper is a gap analysis. We use information from the existing literature to compare neutrinos to the seven DiVincenzo requirements. Firstly, there are five requirements to do with computation and secondly two requirements to do with communication. We analyse where the gaps are for each requirement. Overall, we find that neutrinos have high fidelity and good coherence; however, they do not have a clear qubit definition and initialisation. They do not have universal gates, individual qubit readout, or stationary-to-flying conversion, meaning they either fail or are very poor. Therefore, we think they are best considered as an exceptional flying information carrier; however, they are very difficult to control. We have outlined all of the gaps which can be used to inform future work.

papers.title_en: Helicity-Selective Electron-Phonon Coupling Between $PT$-Partner States in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$
papers.abstract_en: Rotational symmetry ($C_n$) constrains chiral phonons, but how other symmetries affect their interactions remains largely unexplored. We perform a theoretical and computational study of chiral phonon coupling to parity-time ($PT$)-degenerate electron doublets in $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$. Although $PT$ suppresses phonon singlet chirality, chiral phonon doublets can helically interact with $PT$-partner electronic states via a mechanism similar to pseudospin. Selection rules are then analyzed with the interplay of $PT$ and $C_3$. Our computational results of $2H$-bilayer MoS$_2$ suggest chiral phonons may be used to resolve intravalley electronic states in $PT$ systems.

papers.title_en: Heisenberg-Scaling Quantum Metrology of Electron-Photon Coupling via Multi-Electron PINEM
papers.abstract_en: Free-electron quantum optics has recently emerged as a promising platform for coherent electron-light interactions, yet its potential for quantum-enhanced metrology remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the fundamental precision limit of coupling-strength estimation in multi-electron photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), demonstrating that the quantum Fisher information scales quadratically with electron number. We then propose an experimentally accessible scheme combining squeezed-light probing and optical homodyne detection that attains Heisenberg scaling with respect to electron number, provided the electrons exhibit nonzero inter-electron coherence, while surpassing conventional PINEM sensing in photon-number enhancement as well. We further analyze the effect of imperfect electron preparation, showing that electron phase noise is converted into a fluctuating optical displacement and eventually limits the precision. To overcome this limitation, an auxiliary optical mode coupled to the same electron ensemble measures the displacement noise in the signal mode, allowing its conditional suppression and recovery of the Heisenberg scaling. Our work establishes multi-electron coherence as a resource for free-electron quantum metrology and opens the route to precision measurements of nanoscale electron-light interactions.

papers.title_en: "Inevitable'' nonstrange tetraquark states and $ρρ$ interaction
papers.abstract_en: Investigation of the interaction between two $ρ$ mesons with $IJ=00, 02, 11, 20$ and $22$ is conducted systematically in the framework of the quark delocalization color screening model. The results show that there is a strong attractive potential between two $ρ$ mesons, which makes it easier for these two mesons to form bound states. The largest binding energies occur for $IJ=02$ and $IJ=00$ with values over a hundred MeV, while the $IJ=20$ state is the least bound and has a binding energy of only a few MeV. Moreover, the results of intercluster distances favor a molecular interpretation of these states. The interaction analysis reveals that the $ρρ$ and $ΔΔ$ interactions share certain similarities. Drawing inspiration from the $d^*$ dibaryon prediction and from decay-property analyses, we suggest that the $ρρ$ with $IJ=02$ may be the most promising candidate of the ``inevitable'' nonstrange tetraquark state, which deserves experimental search.

papers.title_en: Beam performance and data-constrained optical modeling of a UV-transmitting acrylic Cherenkov counter for hadron identification
papers.abstract_en: A threshold Cherenkov counter based on ultraviolet-transmitting (UVT) acrylic has been developed for hadron identification in the S-2S spectrometer at J-PARC. Three 730 mm $\times$ 100 mm $\times$ 50 mm radiators were beam tested: polished UVT acrylic without WLS, UVT acrylic roughened on the four long surfaces without WLS, and polished UVT acrylic containing 10 ppm by mass bis-MSB as a wavelength shifter (WLS). The polished/WLS prototype gave the largest two-ended photoelectron yield among the tested configurations. At a 1-photoelectron software-SUM threshold, its measured detection efficiency remained above 99% throughout the scanned longitudinal range, with no significant degradation up to an average extracted-particle rate of approximately $2.5\times10^{5}~{\rm s^{-1}}$ during beam delivery. Beam observables constrained a Geant4 optical model with one common detector response scale and no PMT-specific response tuning. The model reproduces the observed response hierarchy and main longitudinal trends. In the central |y| < 200 mm region, simulated and measured MPV estimators for the calibration configurations typically agree within about 15%, while larger deviations occur toward the radiator ends, especially for rough/no-WLS. With the calibrated parameters fixed, the model was used to compare unmeasured detector configurations and quantify the momentum dependence of $K^{+}$/p discrimination. In the central, normal incidence geometry, a 90% $K^{+}$-survival working point is predicted to keep proton survival below 3% up to about 1.8 GeV/c. The measurements and constrained extrapolations support the polished UVT/WLS configuration for S-2S and quantify its expected particle-identification reach beyond the simple threshold regime.

papers.title_en: Modulation and protection of entanglement in a two-qubit system via two interacting oscillator control
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the control and protection of two-qubit entanglement through engineered interactions between two auxiliary harmonic oscillators. Each qubit is coupled to a local oscillator via a dephasing interaction, while the oscillators interact through independently tunable position-position and momentum-momentum couplings. Employing the characteristic-function representation, we obtain analytical solutions for the composite-system dynamics and examine how the stability properties of the coupled oscillators determine the evolution of two-qubit concurrence. Our analysis reveals distinct dynamical regimes exhibiting entanglement revivals, suppression, or decay, and identifies configurations in which oscillator interactions effectively reduce entanglement degradation. We further investigate the influence of thermal dissipation using local and global master-equation descriptions, demonstrating that suitable oscillator couplings can preserve substantial two-qubit entanglement under the dissipative conditions considered. These results establish a connection between the dynamical stability of auxiliary bosonic modes and the controllability of entanglement in discrete-variable quantum systems, providing a potential strategy for entanglement protection through engineered oscillator interactions.

papers.title_en: Measure of set coherence
papers.abstract_en: Set coherence is a quantum resource for a set of states that characterizes whether a collection of quantum states contains coherence, namely whether these states fail to be simultaneously incoherent in a common basis. In this work, we show that the free operations of set coherence are common commutativity-preserving quantum channels, from which we then establish an axiomatic framework for set-coherence measure (SCM). Within this framework, we investigate the robustness based measures deduced by taking, respectively, the average, maximum, and sum of the single-state robustnesses over a common reference basis, where the first two were previously introduced in the literature and we check here whether they satisfy our SCM axioms. Consequently, we show that the averaged robustness is an SCM but it is neither unified nor complete, the maximal robustness is a unified SCM but is neither complete nor strongly superadditive, whereas the sum robustness is a complete SCM. Furthermore, we propose several classes of SCMs based on pairwise commutators. We show that the Schatten $p$-norm based SCMs are complete and strongly superadditive. We also find that the universal fourth-order Bargmann gap measure proposed in the literature is a complete and strongly superadditive quantifier of set coherence. Finally, we discuss the operational meaning of the SCM in the context of optimal approximate quantum broadcasting, and show that the amount of set coherence can closely reflect the performance of this task.

papers.title_en: The Pion Parton Distribution Puzzle in the High x Region
papers.abstract_en: We developed a new theoretical approach in the description of partonic structure of hadrons based on spectral function representation of valence quarks. In this approach massless valence quarks are considered in the mean field of residual hadron. This approach initially was applied to the calculation of parton distribution function~(PDF) of nucleons that resulted in an observation of pion-cloud structure of nucleon. In this report we present our calculation of pion PDF in the valence region within the same approach. In this approach we describe the soft partonic structure of pion through the valence $q\bar q$ cluster, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The pion PDF is calculated using phenomenological Light-Front wave functions for the $q\bar q$ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF~(xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the $q\bar q$ cluster and the mass of the residual system. These parameters are evaluated by fitting the calculated PDF to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF at starting $Q_0$. They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed in the pion to describe existing pion PDFs in the valence region. They also require the $q\bar q$-cluster to be highly virtual with the interacting quark carrying almost all of the momentum of the $q\bar q$ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF. The calculation practically describes the $\sim (1-x)$ behavior observed recently at $x\to 1$ limit. Our non-trivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at $x\to 1$ limit.

papers.title_en: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
papers.abstract_en: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules ($v$ = 0, J = 0 $\rightarrow$$v$ = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 $μ$m. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the $v$ = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain ($λ$ > 4.5 $μ$m) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

papers.title_en: Analysis of $S$-wave $ωπ$ dynamics behavior in multi-body $B_{\ell4}$ and $B_{\ell6}$ decays
papers.abstract_en: The $b_1(1235)$ state has a sizable decay width, which have longstanding puzzle in treating as a final state in theoretical calculations may lead to systematic deviations in the predicted observables. To address this issue and further explore the internal structure of this resonance, we study the multi-body semileptonic decays $B_{\ell4}$ and $B_{\ell6}$. Within the approximation where the $b_1(1235)$ resonance dominates, we study the $B_{\ell4}$ decay $B\to b_1(1235)(\toωπ)\ell^+ν_\ell$ in the QCD light-cone sum rules framework. The corresponding transition form factors (TFFs) are calculated by constructing a correlation function with a right-handed chiral current. As the main nonperturbative input for the TFFs calculation, the transverse twist-2 light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) of the $b_1(1235)$ resonance is constructed using the light-cone harmonic oscillator model, and the resulting LCDA exhibits a single-peak behavior. At the large-recoil region, we obtain the TFFs $V_{0, 1, 2}(0)$ and $A(0)$, together with the corresponding TFFs ratios $r_V = 1.530_{-0.016}^{+0.013}$ and $r_2 = 0.553_{-0.015}^{+0.012}$. We then further study the complete $B_{\ell4}$ decay by incorporating the $b_1(1235)\toωπ$ resonant line shape and obtain the corresponding observables. The results show that the branching ratio of the $B_{\ell4}$ decay is about $1/3$ of that obtained when $b_1(1235)$ is treated as a final state. We also account for the subsequent decay $ω\to π^+π^-π^0$ and further predicted the branching ratio of the $B_{\ell6}$ decay $B\to b_1(1235)(\toω(\to π^+π^-π^0)π)\ell^+ν_\ell$. These results may provide useful references for future experimental measurements and further theoretical studies.

papers.title_en: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
papers.abstract_en: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

papers.title_en: Exact flavor conservation at the quark level in causal clusters: strange particles, protons and light nuclei in small collision systems
papers.abstract_en: The suppression of strange hadrons in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC, including the $ϕ$ meson, has recently been described by the exact conservation of strangeness imposed on the quarks of a causally connected cluster before hadronization. Here we extend this approach to the light flavors. The numbers of up and down quarks and antiquarks are conserved in the same cluster, and the suppression of a baryon or a nucleus depends only on how many light quarks of each flavor it contains. With the strangeness sector fixed by the previous analysis, a single constant, the ratio $r$ of light to strange quark abundances, determines the multiplicity dependence of protons, deuterons, He and hypertriton in pp and p--Pb collisions. Including the finite size of the nuclei, one obtains a very good fit of the data for $r=3.76\pm0.38$, i.e. strange quarks about 0.27 times as abundant as light quarks per flavor, close to the value known from string fragmentation

papers.title_en: Light top-flavoured dark matter in dark SMEFT: one-loop matching and phenomenology
papers.abstract_en: We study light top-flavoured dark matter (DM) below the electroweak (EW) scale within the dark Standard Model effective field theory (DSMEFT). We perform the one-loop matching of the DSMEFT onto the dark low-energy effective field theory (DLEFT) at the EW scale for all relevant operators that couple scalar, fermionic or vector DM, as well as axion-like particles, exclusively to third-generation quarks. After QCD evolution to the relevant low-energy scales, we match the DLEFT onto the non-relativistic EFT for DM-nucleus scattering. This EFT chain provides a unified framework for phenomenological studies of rare $B$- and $K$-meson decays with missing energy, direct and indirect detection, and the thermal relic abundance. Interpreting the Belle II excess in $B^+\to K^+ν\barν$ as a decay into DM, we find that only the DSMEFT operators contributing at tree level can accommodate it with $O(1)$ couplings for a new-physics scale of $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$. The decay $B^0\to K^{*0}+\mathrm{inv}$ provides the strongest constraint over large portions of the Belle II-favoured parameter space, while $K^+\toπ^++\mathrm{inv}$ can dominate at low and $B_s\to\mathrm{inv}$, $B^+\toπ^++\mathrm{inv}$ and $Υ(1S)\to\mathrm{inv}$ become important at high DM masses, respectively. Direct-detection searches by CRESST-III and DarkSide-50 are competitive for operators involving scalar quark currents and, depending on the operator, exclude the Belle~II-favoured band for $m_{\mathrm{DM}}\gtrsim1$-$2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. We also perform detailed analyses of the thermal relic abundance and the indirect-detection constraints from the CMB and Fermi-LAT.

papers.title_en: Charge-Coupled Device-Based Arbitrary Waveform Generation for Qubit Control
papers.abstract_en: We propose an arbitrary waveform generation architecture based on charge-coupled devices (CCDs) for qubit control. Waveform samples are stored as charge packets in CCD channels and sequentially clocked out as voltage samples. Multiple channels are operated in parallel and time-interleaved to achieve high effective sampling rates. The generated baseband waveforms are then upconverted to microwave frequencies to drive qubit operations. By representing waveform information as stored charge rather than as continuously generated or transmitted microwave signals, the proposed architecture provides a path to reducing cryogenic interconnect density and lowering heat load in scalable quantum control systems.

papers.title_en: Photometric Redshift Estimation with Hybrid Quantum Neural Network
papers.abstract_en: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network (HQNN) is applied to recover the photometric redshift of a galaxy dataset built using data from two astronomical surveys, the Kilo-Degree Survey (KIDS) and the VISTA Kilo-Degree Infrared Galaxy (VIKING), which provide data with coverage from the optical to the near-infrared electromagnetic spectrum. The results are then compared with those obtained by a classical neural network. We see that HQNN consistently recovers the reference photometric redshift with a high statistical fidelity. Furthermore, both the $R^2$ and the MSE found by the HQNN are consistently better than those found by the classical counterpart (albeit consistent in the error range), proving the worth of further investigating these novel technologies for this particular astrophysical application.
